segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Let's start the review of Tuesday night's checkout outage. Blameless as always, we're here to fix the system.

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: I'll give the timeline. At 9:42 pm the error rate on checkout jumped to about sixty percent.

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: The database connection pool was full. Every new request waited, then timed out.

segments.speaker: Emily Carter
segments.text: The first alert fired at 9:51, so nine minutes after it started.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Why nine minutes?

segments.speaker: Emily Carter
segments.text: The alert only watches the error rate over a ten minute window. Nothing watches the pool itself.

segments.speaker: Prakash Iyer
segments.text: Support had the first merchant complaint at 9:46. We knew before the pager did.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: That's painful to hear, but useful. Zoya, how did we recover?

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: I raised the pool limit from 50 to 120 at 10:14 and restarted the service. Errors dropped in two minutes.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: So about forty minutes of real impact.

segments.speaker: Prakash Iyer
segments.text: Around three hundred merchants saw failed payments. Most retried, some lost the sale.

segments.speaker: Emily Carter
segments.text: What filled the pool in the first place?

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: A new report query from the 6 pm deploy. It held connections for twenty seconds each.

segments.speaker: Emily Carter
segments.text: And that deploy went out with one approver, late in the day.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Okay. First question: do we keep the pool at 120?

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: The database can take it, I checked CPU and memory headroom yesterday.

segments.speaker: Emily Carter
segments.text: 120 gives us room for spikes. I'd keep it.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Then we keep the connection pool limit at 120 permanently.

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: I'll make sure the config file matches, it's only a runtime change right now.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Second: the deploy. A big query change went out with a single approval at 6 pm.

segments.speaker: Emily Carter
segments.text: I'd like a rule that every checkout deploy needs a second approver.

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: It slows us down a bit, but after Tuesday I agree.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Done. From now on any deploy to the checkout service needs two approvers.

segments.speaker: Prakash Iyer
segments.text: Can we also stop evening deploys altogether?

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: That would block urgent fixes too. I wouldn't go that far.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Let's not ban evening deploys. Two approvers covers most of the risk.

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: On the monitoring gap, I'll add an alert when pool usage crosses eighty percent.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: When can that be live, Zoya?

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: It needs a dashboard change too. I'll have the pool alert live by next Wednesday.

segments.speaker: Emily Carter
segments.text: Note the quarterly load test is on 19 November, the alert should be in before that anyway.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Good, that gives us a real test of it.

segments.speaker: Prakash Iyer
segments.text: What about the merchants? They want to know what happened, and some want money back.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: We offered a fee credit in incidents like this before.

segments.speaker: Prakash Iyer
segments.text: Yes, one day of transaction fees waived.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Then we waive one day of fees for the affected merchants.

segments.speaker: Prakash Iyer
segments.text: Who sends the emails? It shouldn't be a template, it should explain the outage.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Someone needs to email the affected merchants about the credit within 3 days.

segments.speaker: Prakash Iyer
segments.text: My people are swamped with tickets from Tuesday, so not me personally.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Understood. We'll find the right person after this call.

segments.speaker: Emily Carter
segments.text: I'll write a runbook for connection pool exhaustion, so on-call knows what to do next time.

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: Include the restart command, it isn't obvious.

segments.speaker: Emily Carter
segments.text: Will do, with the exact steps from Tuesday.

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: One bigger idea. We could move to a managed database service, they handle pooling for us.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: That's a quarter of work and a big cost change. Not something we decide from one incident.

segments.speaker: Emily Carter
segments.text: Agreed, let's not take that on now.

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: Fine, I'll drop it for now.

segments.speaker: Prakash Iyer
segments.text: Will we publish the post-mortem publicly?

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: A short version on the status page, yes. The full one stays internal.

segments.speaker: Emily Carter
segments.text: The report query itself, is it switched off?

segments.speaker: Zoya Khan
segments.text: Yes, rolled back on Wednesday morning. It comes back only after it's rewritten.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Good. Anything we missed?

segments.speaker: Prakash Iyer
segments.text: Just that support needs a direct line to on-call. We waited for the pager.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Fair point, let's take it up in next week's ops meeting.

segments.speaker: Nikhil Bansal
segments.text: Thanks everyone. Good, honest review.

decisions.fact: The database connection pool limit stays at 120.
Checkout service deploys need two approvers.
Affected merchants get one day of transaction fees waived.

action_items.fact: Zoya adds an alert on connection pool usage above 80%.
The affected merchants are emailed about the outage and credit; no owner was named.
Emily writes a runbook for connection pool exhaustion.

distractors.fact: Moving to a managed database service was suggested and dropped.
Banning evening deploys was suggested and rejected.
19 November is the quarterly load test, not the alert's due date.
